teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies of suspected heatstroke in Japan
teams.body: Fijian rugby is mourning the tragic passing of back-row forward Saimoni Vunilagi, who died in hospital earlier this month after developing severe heatstroke symptoms. The 26-year-old fell ill following a Kyushu KV training session in Fukuoka, where temperatures reached 35C. The Japanese second-division club expressed their profound grief, stating they are "devastated by this sudden news" and paying tribute to Vunilagi's "generous spirit and powerful style of play" after he recently joined the side.

lead.why: The tragic and sudden death of Fijian player Saimoni Vunilagi from suspected heatstroke is the most significant and widely reported news.

teams.heading: Jeremy Guscott calls on Steve Borthwick to unleash 'awesome' Henry Pollock
teams.body: Former England centre Jeremy Guscott has urged Steve Borthwick to hand Henry Pollock a starting role, calling the 21-year-old loose forward 'one of the most gifted players we have ever seen as a seven.' Pollock has established himself in the national squad, earning 13 caps, but 12 of those have come as a replacement. Guscott also questioned the omission of Max Ojomoh and called for Borthwick to give coach Lee Blackett more influence if England are to succeed at the next World Cup.

teams.heading: Rugby journalism mourns as Edmund Van Esbeck dies aged 94
teams.body: The Irish rugby community is in mourning following the death of former Irish Times correspondent Edmund ‘Ned’ Van Esbeck at the age of 94. A defining voice for over 30 years, Van Esbeck charted the sport’s evolution from its amateur roots to the professional era. He authored several authoritative texts on the national team and remained a vocal advocate for the game’s unique ability to transcend divisions, famously noting that rugby succeeded where generations of politicians failed to unite the island.

lead.why: The passing of Edmund Van Esbeck is a significant loss to Irish rugby history and journalism.

teams.heading: Alun Wyn Jones returns to Ospreys as a new board director
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones has joined the Ospreys board of directors with immediate effect. The 40-year-old, who made his debut for the region in 2005, returns at a turbulent time as the club navigates the WRU’s controversial proposal to reduce the professional game to three sides. Chairman James Davies-Yandle stated the club was not looking for a figurehead, but a director who understands the organisation from the inside to help drive long-term stability and growth.

lead.why: The return of a high-profile figure like Alun Wyn Jones to a major regional board is the most significant development in Welsh rugby today.

teams.heading: Kieran Read highlights how Argentina exposed Springboks’ defensive rush system
teams.body: Former All Blacks captain Kieran Read has pointed to Argentina’s strategy in Buenos Aires as a potential blueprint for unlocking the Springboks’ rush defence. Despite a narrow loss, Los Pumas successfully created space on the fringes by using chips and cross-field kicks to bypass the heavy defensive pressure in the middle. Read noted that Argentina’s willingness to trust their depth and move the ball quickly against the South African defensive line provided a template for other teams to follow.

teams.body: The Japanese rugby community is in mourning following the death of Kyushu Kyuden Voltex back-rower Saimoni Vunilagi. The 26-year-old passed away after suffering suspected heatstroke during a training session. A minute’s silence was observed in his honour before the recent Test against Australia, where former teammates Kanji Shimokawa and Naoto Saito were in the starting XV. The Japan Rugby League One expressed their condolences to Vunilagi’s family as the nation continues to navigate an exceptionally intense summer of record-breaking heat.

teams.heading: Anton Segner ruled out as Simon Parker joins All Blacks bench
teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has been forced into a late change for the opening Test against South Africa at Ellis Park. Flanker Anton Segner was withdrawn from the squad after presenting with a swollen ankle, which has been assessed as acute inflammatory arthritis. Simon Parker has been named as his replacement on the bench. An All Blacks spokesperson confirmed that Segner's return to play is yet to be determined, leaving Parker to provide loose forward cover for the series opener.

teams.heading: South Africa suffer heavy defeat as New Zealand claim Ellis Park
teams.body: The Springboks’ unbeaten streak ended in frustration at Ellis Park on Saturday, with the visitors securing a 33-16 victory to take the lead in the four-Test series. Despite South Africa enjoying 51% of possession and 61% of territory, the hosts were unable to convert that pressure into points, ultimately losing the turnover count 23 to 13. André Esterhuizen scored the lone try for the home side, with Cheslin Kolbe contributing the remainder of the points through his boot.
